turns.assessment: The S14 interface raised a local critical transmitter-failure alarm at the same time that the far-end S15 receiver lost och194. The subsequent loss of this channel at OCMs along S14→S04→S15, with unchanged amplifier telemetry and unaffected monitoring on the S14 receiver side, is the expected downstream footprint of a failed transmit laser. A whole-card failure is unlikely because trx.och194.z retained valid receive-side monitoring.

proposals.rationale: The local EQPT_TX_FAIL directly identifies the S14 transmitter, while the far-end receiver and both downstream OCMs lost only och194. Stable amplifier measurements and other channels argue against a shared line-system failure.

A card failure could remove the transmitted channel, but it should also take down the unit's receive traffic and silence its monitoring. The unchanged receive-side metrics at trx.och194.z weigh strongly against this.
